title: The Contest for Athens
notes: p2.4 and p3.2: classical temples appear behind Athena at the moment of the contest, centuries too early. Narration says the temples came later ('her temples went up on this rock').
p3.3: the tag is lettered LEGEND?. Card and coda say MYTH. Patch the tag to MYTH.
p3.4: Glauka is drawn under a roofed porch while the caption says the roof was left open. Minor; narration and her bubble ('Look up. No roof.') carry it.
p3.2: the caption 'She has been its goddess ever since' uses a banned phrase. It is lettered, so it stays; narration paraphrases.

panels.visual: Wide view of the bare rock of the Acropolis in ancient times with a small village around it, Athena and Poseidon standing on opposite sides facing each other, sparks of rivalry between their eyes
panels.caption: Athena and Poseidon both wanted this city.
panels.narr: Hoo. Back then this rock was bare, with a few huts round the bottom. Athena and Poseidon both wanted this city. Look at them glaring.

panels.visual: Poseidon raising his trident high, muscles bulging, sea-green hair whipping
panels.caption: Poseidon struck the rock with his trident.
panels.narr: The rule was simple: give the people the best gift, and the city is yours. Poseidon went first, of course. He struck the rock with his trident.

panels.visual: The rock cracking open and a jet of water bursting upward in jagged white spray; astonished villagers
panels.caption: A spring gushed out.
panels.narr: A spring gushed out of solid rock, right up here on the dry hilltop. The villagers stared. Water from nowhere: what a gift.

voice_speech.speaker: Poseidon
voice_speech.text: Water! From a rock! Beat that.

panels.visual: An Athenian cupping the water and tasting it, tongue sticking out in disgust, comic sweat drop
panels.caption: The water was salty. Nobody could drink it.
panels.narr: Then somebody tasted it. The water was salty. He's the god of the sea: what did they expect? Nobody could drink it.

panels.visual: Athena kneeling calmly on the rock pressing a small olive sapling into the soil, owl Glauka on her shoulder
panels.caption: Athena planted an olive tree.
panels.narr: Athena didn't shout. She knelt down and planted an olive tree. I was sitting on her shoulder, so I saw it all.

panels.visual: The olive sapling bursting into a full tree in golden light, leaves flying, villagers gazing up in awe
panels.caption: A gift.
panels.narr: The little tree shot up into a full olive tree, there and then. Olives to eat, oil for the lamps. A gift that comes back every single year.

panels.visual: A crowd of Athenian men and women raising their hands to vote, olive branches in hands, Poseidon sulking in the corner
panels.caption: The people chose the olive.
panels.narr: Then the whole village voted. Salt water you can't drink, or a tree that feeds you for ever? Up went the hands. The people chose the olive.

panels.visual: Athena, crested helmet pushed back, giving a small victorious smile; behind her the new city called Athens glows in light
panels.caption: The city was named for Athena.
panels.narr: So the city was named for Athena: Athens. She didn't cheer. Just a small smile, the way you smile when you knew all along.

panels.visual: Poseidon stomping away into the sea with waves rolling, grumbling expression, trident dragging
panels.caption: Poseidon lost the contest.
panels.narr: Poseidon lost the contest. He did not lose quietly: he stormed back into the sea and, in his rage, flooded the plain to the west.

panels.visual: Athena and her olive tree on the Acropolis, calm and regal, a temple rising in the background
panels.caption: She has been its goddess ever since.
panels.narr: Athena kept the city. She has been its goddess from that day to this, and later her temples went up on this very rock.

panels.visual: Close-up of marks in a rock floor, three trident-shaped holes, a hand pointing at them, an open roof above showing the sky
panels.caption: Under the north porch of the Erechtheion there are marks in the rock.
panels.narr: Now walk to the north porch of the Erechtheion. Under it there are marks in the rock. The Athenians told it like this: Poseidon's trident made them.

panels.visual: Glauka the owl peering at the trident marks with a monocle-like gleam
panels.caption: People said Poseidon's trident made them. The roof above was left open to the sky.
panels.narr: Above them, the roof was left open to the sky. That's a myth: a story the Greeks told, not a thing that happened. But the marks are real. Go and find them.
